tagline: Up the one natural gap from the coastal plain inland.
intro: East of Highway 55 the Riverside Freeway heads up Santa Ana Canyon, the water gap where the Santa Ana River comes between the Santa Ana Mountains and the Chino Hills, and the only natural break in the range between the coastal plain and the Inland Empire. Only the stretch from Highway 55 to the east Anaheim city limit, in the western part of the canyon, is designated scenic. The freeway runs on through Corona to Riverside.

Before the freeway there was a trail. Benjamin Wilson used it in 1845 to reach the valley he named Big Bear, and gold seekers followed it after 1860, until the Santa Ana flood of 1916 washed most of it away.

moments.title: Olive
moments.text: Portolà's party camped near here in July 1769, and Crespí named the spot for the earthquake that struck while they were there, while the soldiers called the river the Rio de Santa Ana.

moments.title: Santa Ana Canyon
moments.text: In the canyon a bicycle path follows the river bank, roughly alongside the freeway in places, and keeps going all the way down to Pacific Coast Highway.

moments.title: Prado Dam
moments.text: An earth-fill dry dam across the river at the Chino Hills, finished in 1941 after the flood of 1938 had made the case for it, waits to catch the Santa Ana's floodwaters.
